slo_title: Understand the concept and benefits of inheritance in Java.

mcq.q: Which type of inheritance is shown when Class C inherits from Class B, and Class B inherits from Class A?
Which of the following represents single inheritance in Java?

options.A: One class inheriting from multiple classes
options.B: A class inheriting from one class only

mcq.answer_text: A class inheriting from one class only

mcq.q: What is the main benefit of using inheritance in Java?
In hierarchical inheritance, which of the following is true?

options.A: Multiple base classes, one derived class
options.B: One base class, multiple derived classes
options.C: Multiple derived classes extending multiple base classes
options.D: Derived classes that are not connected

mcq.answer_text: One base class, multiple derived classes

mcq.q: Which keyword is used in Java to implement inheritance?

sq.q: Explain the concept of inheritance in Java with a simple example.
answer: Inheritance allows a class (subclass) to inherit properties and methods from another class (superclass). Example: class Animal { void sound() { System.out.println("Animal makes sound"); } } class Dog extends Animal { void bark() { System.out.println("Dog barks"); } } Here, Dog inherits the sound() method from Animal.

sq.q: Write a Java code snippet that demonstrates hierarchical inheritance.
answer: class Vehicle { void start() { System.out.println("Vehicle starts"); } } class Car extends Vehicle { void drive() { System.out.println("Car drives"); } } class Bike extends Vehicle { void ride() { System.out.println("Bike rides"); } } Here, both Car and Bike inherit from the common superclass Vehicle.

lq.q: You are designing a software for a school system. All employees share common details like name and ID, but teachers have subjects and students have grades. Design a Java program using inheritance that models this system with appropriate classes. Explain the type of inheritance used and how it simplifies the design.
answer: Java Code: class Person { String name; int id; void displayDetails() { System.out.println("Name: " + name + ", ID: " + id); } } class Teacher extends Person { String subject; void teach() { System.out.println(name + " teaches " + subject); } } class Student extends Person { int grade; void study() { System.out.println(name + " studies in grade " + grade); } } public class SchoolSystem { public static void main(String[] args) { Teacher t = new Teacher(); t.name = "Mr. Ravi"; t.id = 101; t.subject = "Math"; t.displayDetails(); t.teach(); Student s = new Student(); s.name = "Asha"; s.id = 202; s.grade = 10; s.displayDetails(); s.study(); } } Explanation: The base class Person holds common properties: name and id. Teacher and Student are subclasses, adding role-specific behavior (teach() and study()). This is an example of hierarchical inheritance, where multiple subclasses inherit from a single superclass. Benefits: Promotes code reuse by avoiding duplication of common properties. Supports scalability�more roles like Admin, Counselor can be added easily. Enhances clarity and maintainability by modeling real-world relationships.
